name: Beryllium
hint: Light, strong and hiding in a green gemstone.
method: Leach beryl, convert to the fluoride, reduce with magnesium.

name: Boron
hint: Borax from the laundry aisle holds a brown powder with a green flame.
method: Borax to boric acid to boron oxide, reduce with magnesium.

name: Fluorine
hint: It etches glass before you even free it. Start with fluorite, and do not use glass.
method: HF from fluorite and sulfuric acid, then electrolysis in molten potassium bifluoride.

name: Argon
hint: A lazy gas hiding in every breath. Liquefy the air and take it apart.
method: Fractional distillation of liquid air (0.93% of air).

name: Scandium
hint: A light silvery metal from a rare Norwegian mineral.
method: Thortveitite to the fluoride, reduce with calcium.

name: Titanium
hint: Rutile sand, chlorine, then molten magnesium under argon.
method: Kroll process: chlorinate rutile, reduce the chloride with magnesium.

name: Vanadium
hint: One metal, four colours. Start with vanadinite.
method: Reduce vanadium pentoxide with calcium or aluminium.

name: Chromium
hint: Thermite is not only for iron. Try chromite.
method: Reduce chromium oxide with aluminium.

name: Manganese
hint: The black powder pyrolusite gives a brittle grey metal.
method: Reduce pyrolusite with aluminium or carbon.

name: Cobalt
hint: The ore that colours glass deep blue. It sticks to magnets.
method: Roast cobaltite, reduce with carbon or hydrogen.

name: Nickel
hint: Roast pentlandite. Green salts, magnetic metal.
method: Roast nickel ore, reduce with hydrogen or carbon.

name: Zinc
hint: Roast sphalerite, add carbon, and catch the metal as vapour.
method: Roast sphalerite to the oxide, reduce with carbon near 1000 C and condense.

name: Gallium
hint: A soft metal that melts in your hand... look in bauxite waste.
method: Electrolysis of bauxite-processing liquor.

name: Germanium
hint: A brittle semiconductor lost in zinc smelter dust.
method: Oxide from zinc-ore residue, reduced with hydrogen.

name: Arsenic
hint: Heat arsenopyrite without air and smell garlic. Then do not breathe.
method: Sublime from arsenopyrite at about 615 C without air.

name: Selenium
hint: Red powder in the sludge under a copper refinery.
method: From copper anode slime: roast, leach, reduce with sulfur dioxide.

name: Bromine
hint: A red-brown liquid waiting in brine. A greener gas can push it out.
method: Chlorine bubbled through brine oxidises bromide.

name: Krypton
hint: One part per million of the air. Run the Air Plant for a long time.
method: Fractional distillation of liquid air (about 1 ppm).

name: Rubidium
hint: A soft metal from lilac mica that melts on a warm day.
method: From lepidolite; reduce the chloride with calcium under argon.

name: Strontium
hint: The red in every firework. Roast celestine.
method: Roast celestine to the oxide, reduce with aluminium.

name: Yttrium
hint: It comes off the column with the rare earths.
method: Separated from monazite or xenotime by ion exchange.

name: Zirconium
hint: Zircon sand, treated like titanium.
method: Kroll-type process from zircon.

name: Niobium
hint: Coltan holds two metals that do not want to part.
method: From columbite-tantalite by fluoride solvent extraction.

name: Molybdenum
hint: A slippery grey mineral that looks like graphite. Roast it.
method: Roast molybdenite to the oxide, reduce with hydrogen.

name: Technetium
hint: No stable form exists. Only the reactor can make it.
method: Extract from irradiated molybdenum targets.

name: Ruthenium
hint: In the sludge left after aqua regia has eaten the platinum.
method: Selective precipitation from platinum-group residue.

name: Rhodium
hint: A rose-coloured salt hides the most corrosion-proof metal.
method: Selective precipitation from platinum-group residue.

name: Palladium
hint: It drinks 900 times its own volume of hydrogen.
method: Selective precipitation from platinum-group residue.

name: Silver
hint: A bright bead left in a bone-ash cup when the lead is gone.
method: Cupellation of lead-silver ore.

name: Cadmium
hint: It boils off first when zinc is smelted.
method: Distils off during zinc smelting (boils at 767 C).

name: Indium
hint: So soft it cries when you bend it. Zinc smelters throw it away.
method: Electrolysis of zinc smelting residue.

name: Tin
hint: Cassiterite and charcoal in a furnace. Bronze is waiting.
method: Smelt cassiterite with carbon at about 1200 C.

name: Antimony
hint: Roast stibnite. The metal burns blue-white.
method: Roast stibnite to the oxide, reduce with carbon.

name: Tellurium
hint: Also in the anode slime. Its compounds give you garlic breath.
method: From copper anode slime.

name: Iodine
hint: Violet vapour from the sea. Try seaweed ash.
method: Chlorine through iodide solution, or from seaweed ash.

name: Xenon
hint: The rarest of the air gases. The longest distillation run there is.
method: Fractional distillation of liquid air (about 0.09 ppm).

name: Caesium
hint: Golden metal that melts in your hand and hates water more than anything.
method: From pollucite; reduce with calcium under argon.

name: Barium
hint: Heavy spar holds a metal with an apple-green flame.
method: Barite to sulfide to oxide, then reduce with aluminium.

name: Lanthanum
hint: The first band off the column is the last element you expect.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Cerium
hint: Scrape it and it throws sparks.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Praseodymium
hint: Green salts.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Neodymium
hint: The strongest magnets. Pink-violet glass.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Promethium
hint: Not in the sand at all. Ask the reactor.
method: Synthetic: separated from reactor products.

name: Samarium
hint: A pale yellow band.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Europium
hint: It glows red under ultraviolet light.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Gadolinium
hint: Magnetic on a cold day, and it eats neutrons.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Terbium
hint: It glows green under ultraviolet light.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Dysprosium
hint: A heavy band that comes off early.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Holmium
hint: One more band. Keep collecting.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Erbium
hint: Pink salts.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Thulium
hint: The rarest stable one.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Ytterbium
hint: Nearly the first band off the column.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Lutetium
hint: The densest and hardest. It comes off first.
method: Crack monazite sand with acid, then separate on an ion-exchange column.

name: Hafnium
hint: Zirconium has a twin. Separating them takes patience.
method: Solvent extraction or fractional crystallisation from zirconium.

name: Tantalum
hint: The other half of coltan. Very dense, very stubborn.
method: From coltan by fluoride chemistry.

name: Tungsten
hint: The highest melting point of any metal. Start with scheelite.
method: Tungsten oxide reduced with hydrogen, then sintered.

name: Rhenium
hint: Caught in the dust of a molybdenite roaster.
method: Recovered from molybdenite roaster dust.

name: Osmium
hint: The densest thing there is. Its oxide smells, and you should not smell it.
method: From platinum-group residue after aqua regia.

name: Iridium
hint: Second densest, and almost nothing can corrode it.
method: From platinum-group residue after aqua regia.

name: Platinum
hint: Only aqua regia dissolves it. Then a yellow salt, then heat.
method: Dissolve platinum ore in aqua regia, precipitate with ammonium chloride, heat.

name: Thallium
hint: A heavy poison with a green flame, caught in flue dust.
method: From lead and zinc smelter flue dust.

name: Lead
hint: Roast the shiny grey cubes of galena, then add carbon.
method: Roast galena to the oxide, reduce with carbon.

name: Bismuth
hint: Cool it slowly and it grows rainbow staircases.
method: Smelt bismuthinite, or recover from lead refining.

name: Polonium
hint: A tenth of a milligram per ton of ore. Or ask the reactor.
method: Trace in uranium ore residue, or irradiate bismuth.

name: Astatine
hint: Too rare to see. Hit bismuth with alpha particles and be quick.
method: Cyclotron: alpha particles on bismuth, fast separation.

name: Radon
hint: Seal radium in a jar and wait for a heavy, invisible gas.
method: Collect the gas given off by radium or uranium ore.

name: Francium
hint: You will never see it. Listen for it in the decay of actinium.
method: Trace decay product of actinium (half-life 22 minutes).

name: Radium
hint: It glows, it heats itself, and it hides in pitchblende waste.
method: Co-precipitate with barium from uranium ore residue; fractional crystallisation.

name: Actinium
hint: It glows blue on its own. Look down the radium chain.
method: From uranium ore decay chains, or irradiate radium.

name: Thorium
hint: What made old gas lanterns glow white. It is in monazite waste.
method: From thorianite or monazite residue.

name: Protactinium
hint: A trace within a trace, in uranium ore residue.
method: Trace separation from uranium ore residue.

name: Uranium
hint: A black, heavy ore called pitchblende. Its salts glow green under UV.
method: Pitchblende to yellowcake to metal.

name: Neptunium
hint: The first element past uranium. The reactor makes it.
method: Reactor irradiation of uranium, separated in the hot cell.

name: Plutonium
hint: Made in the reactor, handled only in the hot cell.
method: Reactor irradiation of uranium, separated in the hot cell.

name: Americium
hint: Look up. There is some on the break room ceiling.
method: Americium-241 source from a smoke detector, opened in the hot cell.

name: Curium
hint: More neutrons. Then more.
method: Successive neutron irradiation in the research reactor.

name: Berkelium
hint: More neutrons still.
method: Successive neutron irradiation in the research reactor.

name: Californium
hint: A metal that throws neutrons by itself.
method: Successive neutron irradiation in the research reactor.

name: Einsteinium
hint: Only a microscopic trace, after a very long irradiation.
method: Long reactor irradiation chains.

name: Fermium
hint: The last element a reactor can reach.
method: Long reactor irradiation chains.

name: Mendelevium
hint: A few atoms at a time, from the cyclotron.
method: Ion-beam synthesis on an actinide target.

name: Nobelium
hint: A few atoms at a time, from the cyclotron.
method: Ion-beam synthesis on an actinide target.

name: Lawrencium
hint: The last actinide. Known only by its decay.
method: Ion-beam synthesis on an actinide target.

name: Rutherfordium
hint: A heavy-ion beam, an actinide target, and a detector fast enough to see milliseconds.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Dubnium
hint: A heavy-ion beam, an actinide target, and a detector fast enough to see milliseconds.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Seaborgium
hint: A heavy-ion beam, an actinide target, and a detector fast enough to see milliseconds.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Bohrium
hint: A heavy-ion beam, an actinide target, and a detector fast enough to see milliseconds.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Hassium
hint: A heavy-ion beam, an actinide target, and a detector fast enough to see milliseconds.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Meitnerium
hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

name: Darmstadtium
hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.

hint: A longer beam run. Prove it by its chain of alpha decays.
method: Heavy-ion fusion in the cyclotron, identified by its alpha-decay chain.
